en: The *Vajrāyuṣa-dhāraṇī-sūtra-vidhi*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Great Eloquence,
Rectitude, and Vast Wisdom, who was promoted to the rank of Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial by Imperial Decree.
At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata,
having attained perfect enlightenment at the summit of the fourth dhyāna in the Peak of the Realm of Form,
descended from the peak of Mount Sumeru.
Within the Vajra-jewel pavilion,
all Tathāgatas throughout the entirety of space and the whole dharma-realm gathered like clouds,
surrounding him on all sides, both in front and behind.
With one voice and in unison, they said:
"We pray only that the World-Honored One will turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, most profound and secret—
namely, the Vajradhātu-cakra."
The Wheel of the Command of Trailokyavijaya,
the Wheel of Universal Subjugation,
and the Wheel of the Accomplishment of All Aims.
These four wheels emerge from the heart of Vairocana.
Each wheel contains thirty-seven noble beings,
each with their respective mantra and samādhi.
Each mudrā, ritual gesture, and code of conduct,
through the power of great compassionate vows,
[is manifested] within defiled buddha-fields.
In the Pure and Wondrous World,
they manifest or remain hidden as they turn the wheel of Dharma to bring benefit and happiness, delivering all sentient beings in various and distinct ways.
After Vairocana Buddha had received the requests of all the Tathāgatas and was about to turn the wheel of Dharma, he...
He immediately entered samādhi and beheld Maheśvara, the Great Lord,
who was stubborn and difficult to transform, clinging tenaciously to false views.
"My body of peaceful great compassion is not capable of subduing him.
Thereupon, the Blessed One entered the samādhi of compassionate wrath.
From the center of his chest, he manifested the five-peaked vajra, the Great Bodhicitta.
From [the heart] flows forth the body of the Vajrasattva Trailokyavijaya, with four faces and eight arms, blazing with majestic power, wondrous and difficult to behold;
he prostrates himself before the Tathāgata Vairocana and all the Buddhas.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will instruct me as to what I should do.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya:
"You have now subdued those great devas who were difficult to tame,
causing them all to take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha and to resolve upon bodhicitta.
Immediately thereafter, you subdued all the devas.
Everyone took refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha;
only Mahādeva, possessing extraordinary majesty and power, rose up in opposition.
The Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya subdues various sufferings even unto death; he tramples upon Mahādeva with his left foot and upon Mahādevī with his right. Thereupon, Vairocana Tathāgata...
Having entered the samādhi of Great Compassionate Wrath,
he then spoke the Vajra Life Span Dhāraṇī.
He further entered the Vajra Life Span Samaya.
Furthermore, by binding the secret mudrā and empowering Maheśvara Deva-rāja,
he was restored to life and his lifespan was further increased;
he took refuge in all Buddhas and resolved to attain bodhicitta.
Through empowerment and prophecy, one realizes the eighth stage.
The mantra of Vajrāyus is: Oṃ vajrayuṣe svāhā. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajradhara: "If there are good sons or good daughters..."
If one receives, maintains, and recites this mantra three times every day— one thousand times at each session—

then all karmic causes and conditions for short life and premature death from the past and present will be purified through the power of maintaining this mantra, and one's faith will become clear and pure.
Karmic obstacles will be extinguished and one's lifespan will further increase.
If there are those who practice samādhi,
they shall not undergo rebirth in a physical body produced by their parents during this present life.
Having attained the five supernormal powers, one soars freely through the air.
Next, the gateways of samādhi are explained:
sit in the full lotus posture, close the eyes, and straighten the body.
Place the two hands one above the other or in the mudrā of concentration at the lower abdomen.
Visualize all the Buddhas throughout the expanse of space with perfect clarity.
One should then visualize, within one's own body at the position of the heart,
a pure full moon, brilliant and translucent,
upon which rests the form of a five-pronged vajra.
The blazing light gradually expands until it is equal in size to one's own body,
transforming into the Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya-vajra,
with Vairocana Tathāgata upon his crown.
From every pore of the Buddha’s entire body,
white nectar emerges and flows into one's own body.
Next, one should again visualize within the heart.
The Bodhisattva Vajrasattva possesses supreme marks and signs and is sovereign in majestic power.
Next, one binds the secret mudrā of the empowerment armor of Vajra-life.
Each forms a vajra-fist with both hands;
placing the right thumb over the left,
they hook them together and rest them upon the crown of the head.
Then, recite the Āyus-mantra seven times;
place it before the forehead, separate the hands, and tie them around the neck.
Once the neck has been tied:
Straighten and extend the advancing force, rotating like a ring;
reaching down to the heart, they wind around like the manner of fastening armor,
and then reach behind the back to bind them once more.
It comes to the navel, the two knees, and the lower back;
then to the heart, the two shoulders, the crown of the head, and the area behind the crown.
It further reaches the forehead, where it is tied double behind the neck.
Forming the vajra-fist, gradually lower both hands, slowly descending them in the manner of hanging ribbons.
While reciting the mantra, one accomplishes the donning of armor to protect the body; the mantra for donning the armor is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-yoga. By the power of the empowerment of this secret mudrā, one’s body becomes as firm and indestructible as a vajra.
Free from all calamities and misfortunes, those who behold it rejoice;
all people develop great reverence.
Next, the secret method of homa is explained.
That is to say: the removal of calamities, the prolongation of life, the increase of prosperity, auspiciousness, abundance, and unimpeded eloquence;
and even [protection against] such difficulties as epidemics, wind, and rain.
By performing according to the ritual, all aspirations will be fulfilled.
There are four types of homa altar methods:
namely, square, circular, triangular, and lotus-shaped.
Each person shall sit according to their respective position as requested.
The image of the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā) shall be drawn according to the ritual rules.
The procedures for anointing the maṇḍala are as described in other sections.
I shall now briefly explain the method for constructing a mandala to eliminate calamities and prolong life.
One should thoroughly purify a single room by digging it to a depth of one cubit (*hasta*),
removing all foul, impure things such as ashes, bones, shards, and stones.
Fill it with pure earth.

Construct a square altar measuring three cubits in width, adorned with *gomaya* so that its surface resembles a polished mirror. When digging the ground, if other precious objects are found, [retain them].
This is a mark of great auspiciousness and excellence;
whatever aspirations one seeks shall be swiftly fulfilled.
Should there be any other [such] things...
One should take pure earth from a riverbank to fill it, leveling and smoothing it according to the ritual rules.
One should repeatedly smear it with various fragrant substances mixed with cow dung (*gomaya*).
At the center of the mandala, one should use white powder.
Construct a vajra armor one and a half cubits in size;
in its center, pierce a fire pit one cubit deep,
or half a cubit deep as appropriate.
If one is unable to pierce it,
it is also permissible to take a fire-pit and place it at the center of the altar.
Regarding the positions for the mudrās and the arrangement of flowers, perform them according to their respective locations.
Once the altar has been established, hang various banners and canopies.
Install images of the Vajra Buddhas of the Three Ages and arrange offerings of flowers, fruits, food, and drink around the perimeter of the altar.
Place the substances for the homa before the practitioner.
Furthermore, place four vases at the four corners of the mandala.
Facing the Honored One, recite the mantra according to the ritual rules.
First, prepare twenty-one pieces of firewood, each ten finger-widths long and as thick as a thumb;
dip both ends in ghee and burn them in the hearth once the charcoal fire has become intensely blazing.
Recite the mantra for prolonging life while consecrating the firewood;
each time you recite it once, cast one piece into the fire.
Once the fire has become blazingly intense:
Within the blaze of light, visualize an eight-petaled lotus flower;
within its womb, one should visualize the seed-syllable.
Radiant and brilliant, it shines forth, becoming the Great Vajra Life-Buddha Bodhisattva.
Next, with the four-syllable mantra, invite the Bodhisattvas to descend into the maṇḍala and receive the various offerings.
The four-syllable secret mantra is as follows:
Reciting "Jyaḥ Hūṃ Vam Hoḥ," form the half-vajra mudrā with the right hand and sprinkle water on the fire to purify it.
Next, take a vessel and fill it completely with melted ghee.
Take one thousand and eight stalks of *kālānusāri* grass, or even as few as one hundred and eight,
and soak them in ghee while reciting the *Āyur-mantra*.
According to the number of blades of grass,
recite once and cast each one into the fire; once they have all been cast,
[the rite is complete].
Next, burn and cast various incenses, milk, and curdled milk.
Once the prescribed number of recitations has been completed as before,
pour a full ladle of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) into the fire.
The beginning and end are thus.
If one can perform such offerings during the three months of the long fast, or on one's own birth month, or even on one's birthday,
one will be able to eliminate calamities and increase one's lifespan.
Possessing great merit and wisdom, their supreme vows will be fulfilled;
whether traveling or residing, they shall advance in rank and station;
and their wealth and treasures shall all be abundant and entirely accord with their wishes.
If one seeks to obtain a son or daughter, as well as intelligence, one should perform empowerment upon cow’s ghee at the time of a solar eclipse and consume it; one will then succeed.
Alternatively, if one empowers nine-jointed sweet flag (achillea), [one will likewise succeed].
Once the three signs— smoke, warmth, and light— have appeared,
one should take and consume it; immediately one's wishes will be fulfilled,
and one will recite ten thousand words daily with unimpeded eloquence.
If one seeks to soar through the air with mastery over appearing and disappearing,
one should take ox-gallstone and, following the previous ritual procedure without interruption, perform the empowerment.
Once the three signs have appeared, smear it on the feet and apply a dot on the forehead.
Moving freely through space,
one further seeks all other vows;
these may be performed according to one's inclination within other ritual sections.
All shall be fully accomplished without exception; furthermore,
the land shall be peaceful and secure, free from calamities and epidemics,
with wind and rain occurring in their proper seasons, and the people living in peace and happiness.
All worthy and noble ones will protect their bodies.
A detailed exposition of these benefits would be inexhaustible,
as fully described in the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*.
If one performs the rite for pacifying calamities and prolonging life,
one should sit facing north and construct a circular maṇḍala;
one should visualize all the assemblies of noble beings as being entirely white in color.
One should wear white garments and offer white food;
all ritual implements for the offering shall be entirely white, and one should burn aloeswood incense.
This applies when performing rites for increase and prosperity.
Sit facing east. [Visualize] your own body,
the body of the Honored One, the clothing,
as well as the offerings of food, fruit, and ritual vessels.
Burn white sandalwood incense while using all yellow-colored materials.
If performing a rite of subjugation (*abhicāra*),
sit facing south.
One's own body, as well as the clothing and ritual implements of the deity,
should all be entirely deep blue-black in color.
Burn agalloch incense.
If one performs the rite of magnetizing (vaśīkaraṇa),
one should sit facing west;
the body, as well as the attire, implements, and offerings of the deity, [should likewise be directed toward the west].
All are entirely red in color.
The syllables for burning incense such as *sugandha* are the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of Samantabhadra’s longevity-extending mantra.
The Ritual Manual for the *Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, Volume Two of the Vajra Section.
Included in the Great Ming Canon, Section Du.
The Method for Reciting the *Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī*.
Vajrabodhi and the śramaṇa Amoghavajra translated this scripture;
it shares the same original text as this one,
yet it lacks numerous passages due to omissions.
Now, on the fifth month of the fourth year of the Enpō era (the gengyin year of the Tenna period),
which corresponds to the fifth month of the first year of the Tenmei era (the xinchou year).
The three commentaries were based on those collated by the Great Monk Jishaun of Chikaku-in;
their discrepancies were recorded,
and artisans were commissioned to ensure their preservation.
This original manuscript was requested by the three masters— Vairocana-vajra, Ci-jue (Wŏnhyo), and Ji-jung—
and is truly an excellent text.
On the twenty-first night of the eighth month of autumn in the year of Xinyou,
the first year of the Jōwa era,
this was collated by the śramaṇa Kaidō of Sōjiji Temple on Mount Hōzan.
The sixth day of the first month of summer in the Guihai year of the Xianghe era. Compassionate Obedience.
